mechanism_narrative: The continued sharp fall in WORKPLACES mobility will keep weekday shopping trips suppressed, so RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean for four consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES remains below its current level.

mechanism_narrative: A near-zero or positive turn in GROCERY_PHARM signals resumed essential shopping trips that spill over into adjacent retail visits, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses from negative to non-negative week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weekly means after GROCERY_PHARM reaches non-negative territory.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both stay elevated together, people are spending more leisure time near home and will substitute away from retail outings, pushing RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises for four weeks despite PARKS remaining below its current level and RESIDENTIAL remaining above its current level.

mechanism_narrative: A further decline in TRANSIT stations traffic below its already depressed level will constrain access to shopping districts and delay retail recovery, keeping RETAIL_REC lower over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points below the current week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT drops at least 5 additional points from the current week.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS rebounds strongly while WORKPLACES keep falling, discretionary daytime trips are being reallocated to outdoor recreation rather than stores, so retail mobility weakens over one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises while WORKPLACES falls in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within two weeks after a simultaneous rise in PARKS and fall in WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates people are staying home more, which reduces incidental shopping and should keep RETAIL_REC below the prior four-week average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC moves above its last-4-week mean while RESIDENTIAL remains at or above the current week value.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM stays non-negative for two consecutive weeks, it marks a relaxation in household caution that will spill into nearby retail visits and lift RETAIL_REC over the following month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays at or above zero for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean through the next 28 days despite two straight weeks of non-negative GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS combined with a smaller drop in TRANSIT than in WORKPLACES reflects more non-work outings and local circulation, which will first lift retail traffic within one week and then sustain it over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises and TRANSIT stops falling faster than WORKPLACES
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week after PARKS improves and TRANSIT declines less than WORKPLACES.
